To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

after a demanding isometrical contraction protocol, mitochondrial generation of reactive oxygen in skeletal muscle extracelluar space is not the major source of extracellular superoxide anions but is a major source of extracelluar hydroxyl radical.

a 15-min protocol consisting of 180 isometic contractions induced a 2-fold increase in superoxide concentration in the extracular space of muscles from adult mice that was not dependent on mitochondrial superoxide dismutation and a 3-fold increase in hydroxyle radical concentration that was dependent on mitochondrial superoxid dismutation.

, after a 15-min contraction protocol of 180 maximal isometric contractions, the concentration of superoxide in the extracellular muscle space is unchanged in Sod2(+/+), but not Sod2(+), mice, whereas hydroxy radical activity in the same space is unchanged in the Sod2(+/+) mice, but not Sod(+/-) mice.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the generation of reactive oxygen in the extracellular spaces of skeletal muscles and the role of mitochondrial superoxide in this process.
the role of mitochondrial superoxide in the generation of reactive oxygen in the extracellular compartment of skeletal muscle.

the hypothesis that, during a demanding contraction protocol, the increase in superoxide and hydroxy radical concentrations in the extracular space of muscles is due to the mitochondrial generation of superoxides and that, with the reduction in MnSod activity, the increase in concentration of hydroxides is decreased.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the major source of reactive oxygen species generated in skeletal muscle extravesicular space after a demanding contraction protocol is the degradation of hydrogen perioxide generated by MnSod.
the source of superoxide anionic generation in the extracellular muscle space during contraction is not mitochondrial, but the source of hydroxyl radical formation is mitochondrial.

the increase in superoxide concentration in the extrascular space of muscles from Sod2(+) and Sod(2-/-) mice after contraction is most likely not directly related to the increase in superoxides generated by mitochondria but to a more complex process involving the generation of superoxide and hydrogen peroxide and their interaction with iron ions in the extracellular matrix of muscles.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MnSOD is not required for contraction-induced generation of superoxide in skeletal muscle extracelluar space but is required for contraction-induced formation of hydroxyl radical.

, in the extracellular compartment of skeletal muscle, MnSOD is not the major source of extracellular superoxide anions, but MnSOD is the major source of hydrogen peroxide that is converted into hydroxyl radicals.

the major source of reactive oxygen species generation after a demanding isometry contraction protocol is mitochondrial generation of hydrogen peroxide, which is degraded to water by MnSOD, with the resultant increase in hydroxil radical concentration in the muscle extracellular space being the consequence of a reduction in Mn-SOD activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
MnSOD activity is required for generation of hydroxyl radical in the extracellular muscle space after a demanding isometic contraction protocol.
MnSOD plays a major role in the generation of hydroxyl radical from superoxide anion in the extracellular compartment of skeletal muscle.
the contraction-induced generation of hydroxyl radical in the extracellular spaces of skeletal muscles is a MnSOD-dependent process.
